note.text: A journey narrative gives a reader a starting situation, a route, significant events and an ending. Use time connectives and a consistent narrative viewpoint. Describe a few relevant details instead of listing every object seen. Past tenses commonly tell the completed events, while the past continuous can provide background. A story should not promise that an unsafe action is sensible. Invent a journey if you prefer not to share personal travel details.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A journey narrative gives a reader a starting situation, a route, significant events and an ending. Use time connectives and a consistent narrative viewpoint. sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: Last week, an imaginary learner travelled with an aunt from a village to Buea. They waited at a sheltered stop while rain fell. When the bus arrived, they boarded carefully and stored the bag safely. The rain eased on the way, and the learner noticed fields beyond the window. At their destination, the aunt checked the bag before they left the bus.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Plan departure, an event on the way and arrival. Check the order and who each pronoun refers to. Use description to support the story rather than replacing the sequence. End with the journey's outcome or a relevant reflection.

paper_task.prompt: Write an original or imaginary journey account. Present the travellers, a relevant event and the arrival; keep private details fictional.
model: Last week, an imaginary learner travelled with an aunt from a village to Buea. They waited at a sheltered stop while rain fell. When the bus arrived, they boarded carefully and stored the bag safely. The rain eased on the way, and the learner noticed fields beyond the window. At their destination, the aunt checked the bag before they left the bus.
checklist: The reader can follow the sequence.
My viewpoint, pronouns and tenses are clear.
Description supports the story rather than interrupting it.
